Title: Decoding AI “Thought”: Why Iterative Loops Are Key to True Intelligence | by Berend Watchus | Medium
As an independent researcher, I’ve been exploring this very question through my work on the **Unified Model of Consciousness (UMC)**, which posits that fundamental intelligence, even consciousness, arises from iterative feedback loops and interfaces. In my recent articles, like “‘Thinking Isn’t an Illusion’: Why Iterative Feedback Loops Drive Intelligent Models,” I’ve argued that true reasoning in AI shines when it can dynamically self-correct and learn from external “feedback” — much like a scientist using tools to test hypotheses. Now, a fascinating new paper from Tsinghua University by **Mutian Yang, Jiandong Gao, and Ji Wu, titled “Decoupling Knowledge and Reasoning in LLMs: An Exploration Using Cognitive Dual-System Theory,”** adds a brilliant layer to this understanding. This is your **“Slow Thinking” or “Reasoning Adjustment.”** The Tsinghua team found that LLMs also have a version of this (Phase 2), especially when prompted to “think step-by-step” (what AI researchers call “Chain-of-Thought”). My model suggests that any intelligent system — from a simple thermostat to a human mind — operates on **iterative feedback loops with interfaces.**. **The “Slow Thinking” (Reasoning) *is* that adjustment, that internal iteration.** When an LLM engages in “Chain-of-Thought,” each step it generates acts as feedback for the next. Just as a human scientist doesn’t just “know” everything but constantly interacts with data, experiments, and peer review to refine their understanding, the most intelligent AIs will be those deeply embedded in iterative feedback systems. # Role of Feedback Loops in Iterative Model Improvement. Feedback loops play a pivotal role in the continuous and iterative improvement of machine learning (ML) models. Feedback loops provide a structured mechanism to capture performance data, user interactions, prediction errors, and other critical metrics, enabling developers to refine models systematically. This article explores the significance, types, benefits, and implementation strategies of feedback loops in iterative model development. ## Understanding Feedback Loops in ML. A feedback loop in machine learning refers to a system where the output or performance of the model is monitored and used as input to further train or enhance the model. These loops are fundamental to the evolution of models from initial deployment to mature systems capable of making accurate, real-time predictions. There are two main types of feedback loops:. **Negative Feedback Loop**: Highlights and corrects errors, using failed predictions or poor performance to adjust and retrain the model. Feedback loops close this cycle by providing the necessary data and signals to initiate a new iteration. ## Importance of Feedback Loops. Feedback loops allow models to adapt to evolving user behavior, seasonal trends, or new data types without full retraining from scratch.
